data.title: User Flow
data.tagline: A path diagram of the steps and branches a user takes to reach one goal
data.learningOutcome: You can map the entry, key actions, required branches, and endpoints for one goal, and distinguish a user flow from a sitemap, wireframe, or customer journey.
data.description: A sign-up flow might show entering the sign-up page, filling in details, verification success or failure, and account creation. It keeps the steps that affect progress, not every click on the screen.

learning.assumes: You have used a multi-step task such as signing in, booking, or checking out.
learning.outcome: You can map the entry, key actions, required branches, and endpoints for one goal, and distinguish a user flow from a sitemap, wireframe, or customer journey.

explanation.title: Fix the user, goal, and entry
explanation.text: Say who starts where, what they want to finish, and what counts as done.

explanation.title: Connect meaningful actions
explanation.text: Show the pages, actions, and decisions that move the task forward, not every scroll or click.

explanation.title: Add branches and recovery
explanation.text: Show what happens after an unavailable slot, bad details, or failed submission, and how the user returns to the main path.

data.boundary: A sitemap maps page hierarchy, a wireframe maps one screen, and a customer journey spans touchpoints and feelings. A user flow focuses on actions and decisions for one in-product goal.

lessonPractice.title: A team wants to inspect the path for “a visitor completes a booking.” Which diagram is the best User Flow?

options.label: Start at the booking entry, continue through slot selection and details submission, and map available, unavailable, success, invalid-details, and return-to-edit paths
options.feedback: Correct. It centers on one user goal and includes an entry, key actions, decisions, a successful endpoint, and recovery from failure.

options.label: List the hierarchy of Home, Services, Pricing, and Help Center pages without showing booking actions or outcomes
options.feedback: That is sitemap content organization and navigation structure. It does not show how a visitor completes a booking.

options.label: Draw the exact size and position of every input and button on the booking screen without connecting the sequence or error branches
options.feedback: That is closer to a wireframe’s interface layout. Without actions and branches, the complete user path cannot be checked.

data.agentPrompt: Map the User Flow for “a first-time visitor completes a booking.” Use only the rules I provide to show the entry, key actions, branches such as no available slots and invalid details, plus success and recovery endpoints. Ask me about missing business rules instead of expanding this into a site-wide sitemap or detailed wireframe, then walk every branch to check for dead ends.
